option_a_new_definitions_by_purpose.note: the remainder of the diff is in-place branches (the data block, the geometry call, the CLI flags, preflight, the staged command), which no separate definition owns.

option_a_CHOSEN.what: teach train_flagship_v4 to read v2 + bind the geometry
option_a_CHOSEN.new_machinery_note: every capability it uses already existed: build_v2_providers (the v2 loader), assert_v2_parity_cache (the membership proof), apply_geometry_args (the frame), HeldoutGate (the mid-run gate). The diff is wiring and refusals.

option_b_REJECTED.what: port the held-out val loop into train_flagship4b
option_b_REJECTED.floor_not_estimate: counts only existing definitions that would have to move — not the wiring, the tests, the second optimizer group, or the v2 val-cache branch it ALSO needs (which is option A's work done twice).
option_b_REJECTED.why_it_is_not_a_port: train_flagship4b's selected plan is 4 points at 0.5 s spacing (tactical waypoint_horizons (5,10,15,20)); the gate's pseudo-simulation differentiates at dt=0.1 s and raises NonDensePlanError on it. A dense plan means FlagshipV4Head and the loss that trains it — i.e. making 4b into v4.
